We need propose a 3-step retrosynthesis for target: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have hints: step1: sulfonamide formation (amine + sulfonyl chloride). step2: Doebner modification (aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid). step3: amide coupling (acid + amine). So forward order: first sulfonamide formation, then Doebner modification to create the α,β-unsaturated acid side chain, then amide coupling to attach anilide.

But retrosynthetic order is reverse: start from target, break amide to give acid and aniline (Nc3ccccc3N). Then break α,β-unsaturated acid to aldehyde + malonic acid? Actually Doebner modification forms α,β-unsaturated acid from aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid. So retro: disconnect the C=C and C=O to give aromatic aldehyde (c2ccc(??)?) and malonic acid? The product side chain is /C=C/C(=O)N... The α,β-unsaturated acid is attached to aromatic ring via double bond. So retro step: break the C=C and C=O to give aromatic aldehyde (c2ccc(CHO)cc2) and malonic acid? Wait Doebner: aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid (with decarboxylation). So product is unsaturated acid attached to aromatic ring. So retro: unsaturated acid -> aldehyde + malonic acid. So we need template for that.

Then sulfonamide formation: target has NS(=O)(=O) attached to aromatic ring. Retro: break S-N bond to give sulfonyl chloride (Ar-SO2Cl) and aniline (the other aromatic ring with amine). So we need template for sulfonamide formation.

Thus propose route:

Target (mol) -> Reaction1 (amide coupling) -> precursors: (A) aromatic sulfonyl aryl with unsaturated acid (i.e., Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/CO)cc2)cc1?) Wait after breaking amide we get acid: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)O)cc2)cc1 (the acid). And amine: Nc3ccccc3N (para-aminophenyl? Actually it's an aniline with an extra NH2? The amide is C(=O)N c3ccccc3N meaning the amide nitrogen attached to phenyl with an NH2 substituent? The SMILES: C(=O)N c3ccccc3N => anilide where the aniline has an NH2 ortho? Actually c3ccccc3N is an aniline (aniline). So amine is aniline (aniline). So step1: amide coupling of acid (aryl sulfonyl unsaturated acid) with aniline.

Step2: The acid precursor from step1 is derived via Doebner from aromatic aldehyde (c2ccc(CHO)cc2) and malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH). So we need to generate that aldehyde attached to sulfonyl aryl? Actually the aromatic ring bearing sulfonyl group is same as before. So the aldehyde is the same aromatic ring with sulfonyl group attached: c2ccc(CHO)cc2 attached to sulfonyl? Wait the sulfonyl is attached to that ring via S(=O)2 to the first phenyl (the tolyl). The second phenyl (c2ccc(... )cc2) is attached to sulfonyl as well. So the aldehyde is on that second phenyl, which also has the sulfonyl attached. So the aldehyde precursor is Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(CHO)cc2)cc1.

Step3: The sulfonyl chloride precursor is formed from sulfonyl chloride reacting with aniline (the first phenyl with methyl). Actually sulfonamide formation: we need sulfonyl chloride (Ar-SO2Cl) and aniline (the other phenyl). The sulfonyl chloride is derived from the tolyl sulfonyl chloride? Wait the sulfonamide is NS(=O)(=O) attached to the first phenyl (tolyl) and to the second phenyl (the one with unsaturated chain). In target, the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the first phenyl (tolyl) and to the sulfonyl group attached to second phenyl. Actually SMILES: Cc1ccc(N S(=O)(=O) c2ccc(... )cc2)cc1. So the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the tolyl ring (as substituent) and the sulfonyl group is attached to second phenyl. So sulfonamide formation could be between aniline (tolyl- NH2) and sulfonyl chloride (c2ccc(SO2Cl)cc2). So retro: break N-S bond to give tolyl- NH2 (p-toluidine) and sulfonyl chloride attached to second phenyl.

Thus final precursors: p-toluidine (C c1ccc(N)cc1) and sulfonyl chloride aromatic (c2ccc(SO2Cl)cc2) which after Doebner gives aldehyde? Wait sulfonyl chloride aromatic is same as second phenyl with sulfonyl chloride attached (no aldehyde). Then Doebner modifies that aromatic aldehyde, but we need aldehyde not sulfonyl chloride. Actually the aldehyde is on the aromatic ring bearing sulfonyl group. So we need sulfonyl chloride with aldehyde? The sulfonyl chloride is attached to aromatic ring; the aldehyde is also on same ring (para to sulfonyl?). In our target, the aldehyde is not present; after Doebner, the aldehyde becomes unsaturated acid. So retro: unsaturated acid -> aldehyde (same aromatic ring). So the aldehyde precursor still has sulfonyl group attached (since sulfonyl is attached to that ring). So the aldehyde precursor is Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(CHO)cc2)cc1. This can be obtained from sulfonyl chloride (c2ccc(SO2Cl)cc2) reacting with p-toluidine to give sulfonamide, then formylation (e.g., Vilsmeier) to give aldehyde? But we only have three steps allowed. The hints only give three reactions: amide coupling, Doebner, sulfonamide formation. So the aldehyde must be directly available as starting material (commercial). So we can assume aldehyde with sulfonyl group is commercially available. So our three steps: 1) amide coupling (target -> acid + aniline). 2) Doebner (acid -> aldehyde + malonic acid). 3) sulfonamide formation (aldehyde-sulfonyl precursor -> sulfonyl chloride + p-toluidine). Wait order: forward: sulfonamide formation first (makes sulfonamide), then Doebner to create unsaturated acid, then amide coupling to attach aniline. But retrosynthesis order is reverse: break amide, then break unsaturated acid, then break sulfonamide.

Thus we need to find templates for each step. Use search to get template IDs for each transformation.

First, amide coupling: functional_groups_broken: aliphatic carboxylic acid, formed: amide. We attempted earlier but got low similarity. Maybe we can just use template ID from result list? The search gave some templates with retro_smarts. We need template_id (maybe reaction_id?). The JSON expects "template_id": some integer? In example they used numeric. So we can use reaction_id as template_id? Probably template_id is integer. We'll pick the first result's reaction_id 401931 for amide coupling? That template seems to involve amide formation with double bond? Not sure.

Better to search for amide formation specifically. Use functional_groups_broken ["aliphatic carboxylic acid"] and formed ["amide"] again but maybe limit more. Already got result with low similarity but okay.

Second, Doebner modification: functional_groups_broken: aldehydes, carboxylic acid? Actually Doebner forms unsaturated acid from aldehyde + malonic acid, breaking aldehyde C=O and one C-C bond in malonic acid, forming C=C and new C-C bond. So we can search broken aldehydes, formed C-C double bonds. Use functional_groups_broken ["aldehydes"], functional_groups_formed ["C-C double bonds"] we did and got empty. Maybe need "C-C double bonds" is correct. Could be "C-C double bonds" is valid. It returned empty. Maybe need also "carboxylic acid" broken? But malonic acid is carboxylic acid broken. So broken: aldehydes, carboxylic acids. Let's try both.
